sections.name: File setup, fact
sections.title: Test setup and sample fact
sections.what: Imports the review functions and creates one sample research fact about an original budget, marked as a direct, relevant source. No checks run in this part.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared sample means each test changes only one thing.
sections.watch_out: The sample is hand-built and cast to a type, so it can differ from real facts.

sections.name: review
sections.title: Tests for the claim review rules
sections.what: Checks that an exact statement keeps the fact verified, and that paraphrases, unattributed claims, values missing from the statement, failed source checks and failed relevance checks are held out. Also checks that only a reviewed fact is admitted.
sections.why: Likely reason: each gate is pinned so a future change cannot quietly let weak claims through.
sections.watch_out: Some assertions expect the review version to be 1, so bumping that version means updating these tests too.

summary: Tests that the claim review rules admit only exact, attributed and correctly valued statements, and that a positive review cannot override a failed source check.
purpose: Protects the main gate between candidate research facts and the facts the calculations may use.
why: Likely reason: this gate is the main protection against wrong research values entering a calculation.
how: Builds one sample fact about an original budget, then checks several review outcomes: exact statement passes, a paraphrase is held out, unattributed or wrong-value reviews are held out, failed source or relevance checks cannot be overridden, and the admission check agrees with the outcome.
inputs: A fixed sample passage and hand-written review verdicts.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner.
risks: The tests use a hand-built sample and do not call the real AI reviewer, so they show the rules work, not that the reviewer is accurate.
debug: If a test fails, read the failing assertion and compare it with the rules in the semanticPolicy file. The message names the field that changed.
